title: Mixed-precision rollout: fused-op fallback gap causing intermittent crash loops and accuracy drift
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a gradual rollout of the mixed-precision (int8->int4) dynamic conversion feature, approximately 1.8% of in-catalog models triggered a fused-operator pattern (bias + gelu + reshape) that our new int4 kernel path did not recognize. When the runtime attempted the fast path it hit an unhandled op-combination in the code path, which resulted in process crash loops on serving nodes. Simultaneously, a small subset of canary traffic experienced silent accuracy drift due to a fallback that returned int8 quantized kernels without the expected dequant ordering. This ticket captures the post-incident follow-ups, mitigations already applied, root cause analysis, and tracked action items to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2025-02-10 09:05 UTC - Canary rollout started for runtime-1.20 with mixed-precision enabled for 5% traffic
2025-02-10 09:47 UTC - Canary health alerts: 502/503 spikes on two clusters serving specialized transformer variants
2025-02-10 10:02 UTC - Pager escalation: on-call observed repeated worker restarts and OOM logs in /var/log/redwood/runtime.log
2025-02-10 10:15 UTC - Emergency rollback of mixed-precision flag to canary cohort; traffic reverted to int8 path, reducing restarts
2025-02-10 11:30 UTC - Initial mitigation: added defensive op-fingerprint check to skip new fastpath for unknown fused patterns
2025-02-11 14:00 UTC - Postmortem triage meeting: agreed to broaden telemetry, create targeted unit tests, and improve fallback logic consistency
2025-02-13 08:20 UTC - Observed lingering accuracy drift in 0.4% of canary requests traced to dequant order mismatch; added temporary monitoring alert
mitigation: Immediate rollback of mixed-precision fastpath for affected canary cohorts. Deployed a hotfix that adds an opset-fingerprint guard: if fused-op pattern not in approved list, the runtime uses the stable int8 execution path. Added alerting on crash-loop frequency and per-model accuracy delta compared to baseline.
root_cause: Twofold: 1) The mixed-precision kernel selector assumed a canonical op ordering for fused bias+gelu+reshape patterns; a subset of exported models used a non-canonical layout (bias fused after reshape) causing unhandled pattern match and a crash in the int4 optimized path. 2) The fallback mechanism that migrated execution to int8 did a late dequant reorder in a different place in the execution graph, causing token-level numeric differences that accumulated as measurable accuracy drift in edge prompts.
action_items: ENG-43567-A1: Expand fused-op fingerprint registry and add negated tests for non-canonical orderings. Owner: Marco Chen. Estimate: 5. Owner ETA: 2025-02-20
ENG-43567-A2: Harden kernel selector to detect and gracefully skip unsupported fused permutations before scheduling fastpath. Owner: Priya Nair. Estimate: 3. Owner ETA: 2025-02-18

ENG-43567-A3: Standardize dequant placement so fallbacks and fastpath have identical dequant semantics; add cross-path numeric regression tests (token-level diffs). Owner: Liang Zhou. Estimate: 5. Owner ETA: 2025-02-25

ENG-43567-A4: Add per-model canary thresholds and automations to abort rollout when crash-loop > 0.5% or accuracy drift > 0.2% on evaluation prompt set. Owner: Samira Ortiz (SRE). Estimate: 3. Owner ETA: 2025-02-22
ENG-43567-A5: Backfill historical telemetry to find prior occurrences and notify affected customers with potential degraded outputs. Owner: Camille Ruiz (Support). Estimate: 2. Owner ETA: 2025-02-19
ENG-43567-A6: Create a small corpus of synthetic fused-op variants and add them to nightly regression and CI. Owner: Marco Chen. Estimate: 2. Owner ETA: 2025-02-24
acceptance_criteria: All expanded fused-op fingerprints added, and unit tests cover the new permutations
Kernel selector returns stable int8 path for unknown fused patterns with no crashes observed for 7 days in canary
Numeric regression tests show fallbacks and fastpath produce token-delta < 0.1% for guarded prompt set
Automated canary abort triggers on new deployments with crash-loop or accuracy drift thresholds breached
Support notifications sent to customers for any affected model IDs discovered
